label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hvr.mdl, models/crystal.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Every view reads as a control console. It is a cabinet with two doors, a sloped control deck, and an upright screen panel behind the deck. The side views show the slope and the back panel clearly, and nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The measured height is 52 against the 40 the brief asks, 30% off where the limit is 15%. The deck sits at about waist height, but the screen panel makes the whole model clearly too tall. Length 64 and depth 26.5 are reasonable for a console.

M3.reason: Everything the brief asks for is there and in place. The upright panel holds two screens. The deck has three round dials with needles and a row of six switches (white, red and yellow), plus a black readout. The cabinet below has two doors with handles.

M4.reason: The body is grey-green painted metal, the deck and switch strip are dark, and the trim is yellow hazard paint. The screens are green and the dial faces cream. This fits the brief's industrial palette with no neon. The yellow strip and the green screens are saturated but stay within Half-Life's range.

M5.reason: The markings are there: screen traces, red dial needles, a yellow stripe, door seams and handles, a side panel line, and light edges. Wear is thin, though, for a station the brief calls rusted and worn. The paint is clean with only faint mottling, there is no rust or chipping, and the back (BACK, BACK-LEFT, BACK-RIGHT) is a bare flat slab.

M6.reason: In the line-up, A is clearly the odd one out next to B, C and D. Its textures are flat and clean, with simple drawn lines on solid green screens. Valve's photo-sourced crystal, rock and rod have noisier, richer textures. It holds together as a prop, but a player would see it as made by someone else.

M7.reason: The front, with the screens, dials and doors, faces the FRONT camera. The model stands upright on its base, and the BELOW view shows a closed bottom with nothing floating.

M8.reason: The check reports no errors. It has 144 triangles against the limit of 210 (twice the median of 105). No part looks open, inside out or floating in any view.
